transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (CTO, Aegis), Maya Li (ML Eng), Raj Patel (Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve Redwood API quickstart, free credits, and validating time-to-first-token for an inference prototype. Security and hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) briefly discussed; next steps include quickstart link, benchmark checklist, and security docs review.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, priya our solutions engineer is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir: hey thanks yeah doing well, samir here. excited to learn how fast we can get something running, we want time-to-first-token to be like under 200 ms for our demo workload.
[00:18] Priya: awesome hi i'm priya, i'll help with the technical bits. quick question on your current stack — are you experimenting with hosted apis already or self-hosted models?
[00:27] Maya: we have some experiments on openai for prototyping, but ops wants predictable cost for demo env and we're looking at either reserved capacity or private infra.
[00:36] Raj: from security side we need SOC2 compliance and possibly VPC peering for any PII. also SSO/SAML is must.
[00:44] Jordan: great — that's pretty common. our quickstart PLG flow gets you to first token in minutes on the hosted API; you also get free credits to run initial evals. for production you can move to Dedicated or Private depending on isolation needs.
[00:58] Priya: to add — the hosted api is super fast for prototyping; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and consistent throughput, Private gives on-prem or VPC with customer key management (K M S / H S M).
[01:12] Maya: can you give a sense of latency tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated?
[01:18] Priya: yeah so for small evals hosted via our nearest region will typically be 50-150ms per token for the model families you mentioned; Dedicated lowers variance and helps with sustained QPS because you get pinned GPU capacity — percents vary by model and prompt length.
[01:35] Samir: what about cold start and kv cache — will that affect our demo?
[01:40] Priya: there's cold start when the model isn't warmed, but our runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeat prefix token costs; sometimes transcription or notes will show K V cash in exports, sorry that slips in the docs.
[01:52] Raj: can you outline the free credits and pilot limits?
[01:57] Jordan: yes — for PLG signups we provide free credits (typically enough for several thousand API calls) and a sandbox quota; we can temporarily bump quotas for benchmarking tests. i'll send details.
[02:08] Maya: great. for time-to-first-token tests we'll run our usual prompts — single-turn, 512 tokens max, mixed batch sizes. what's your recommended test harness?
[02:18] Priya: we'll share a benchmark checklist and sample payloads. common pattern: run 50 cold requests, then 500 steady-state to capture p95/p99. include streaming latency if you plan to use streaming.
[02:31] Samir: any gotchas on model compatibility? we use some distilled open models and a custom fine-tune internally.
[02:37] Priya: Redwood supports a catalog of open models and we also support bringing your own artifacts in Private. for hosted we have curated variants and automatic rollback; for custom models Private is easiest.
[02:48] Jordan: curious — what's your timeline and success criteria for this eval?
[02:52] Samir: timeline is 4-6 weeks, success criteria are: sub-200ms median generation for short prompts, predictable cost under $X per 1k tokens, and security signoff.
[03:05] Raj: and we need audit logs retained for 90 days, SAML SSO, and IP allowlist.
[03:12] Priya: we have audit logs and retention options in the console and SAML is supported; for retention beyond standard tiers that's an add-on but we can share the package.
[03:22] Maya: does the quickstart require an agent or CLI? we prefer to script everything in CI.
[03:28] Jordan: quickstart has both — a one-click console flow and an SDK/CLI path. time-to-first-token from code is typically under 10 minutes if you have API key and network ready.
[03:40] Priya: small note — sometimes customer firewalls require outbound to specific domains; we'll include domain allowlist for the hosted endpoints in the docs.
[03:50] Samir: any benchmarking you've published against Sagemaker or others?
[03:55] Priya: we have internal perf profiles and publicized some benchmarks; i'll include a lightweight comparison and recommended models per latency vs cost.
[04:05] Raj: encryption — at-rest and in-transit? key management?
[04:09] Jordan: all hosted data is encrypted in-transit and at-rest; for Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. we'll pass SOC2 and encryption docs.
[04:18] Maya: curious about pricing — per-token vs dedicated commit. initial prototyping cost matters to product team.
[04:25] Jordan: for PLG hosted it's usage-based per token/embedding; Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity which helps at scale. we'll send an example cost model based on your projected QPS.
[04:36] Samir: for the demo we want to run at ~10 TPS for 20 minute bursts, and sustain 2-3 TPS normally.
[04:44] Priya: Dedicated burst capacity can handle that with predictable tail latencies; hosted can if region capacity is available but Dedicated reduces risk of throttling.
[04:55] Raj: compliance review — can we get a security package to review with our legal?
[05:00] Jordan: yes, i'll attach SOC2, encryption whitepaper, and the SAML/SSO integration guide.
[05:06] Maya: excellent. would you also provide an example of the quickstart script so our CI can call it?
[05:11] Priya: i'll include a sample Node and Python snippet plus curl. time-to-first-token example included.
[05:18] Jordan: ok let's talk pilot flow — you sign up via PLG, we provision free credits, you run benchmark tests, then we decide if you want Dedicated or Private for production.
[05:29] Samir: sounds good. question — if we start on hosted and later move to private, is migration straightforward?
[05:36] Priya: yes we've built the deployment abstraction so you keep API surface; model pinning and rollout policies transfer, but Private will require infra provisioning and KMS setup so timeline is a couple weeks.
[05:49] Raj: any NDA or contractual steps?
[05:52] Jordan: for pilot usually no NDA but if you need one we can escalate. enterprise contracts for Dedicated/Private handled later.
[05:59] Maya: OK what's the expected next step timeline?
[06:02] Jordan: we'll send docs and the quickstart link today/tomorrow. after you sign up we'll schedule the SE-led deep dive and ramp quotas for benchmarking.
[06:12] Samir: good — we'll try to run initial tests next week.
[06:15] Priya: one more technical note — if you plan to use streaming and function/tool calling, share sample payloads because that impacts kernel selection and batching strategies.
[06:26] Maya: noted, we'll share our demo prompts and expected max tokens.
[06:30] Jordan: wrap up — recap of next steps and owners. Jordan sends quickstart, Priya sends benchmark checklist, Samir shares QPS numbers and prompts, Raj shares compliance contacts. schedule deep dive for next week.
[06:45] Raj: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[06:48] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up.

(Transcript continues with brief clarifications and crosstalk, total duration ~42 minutes)
